dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: An indexed mixed-precision rounding model. By D011, it contains input and accumulation formats, compatible exponent and precision ranges, and input and accumulation rounding functions with relative-or-absolute error decompositions.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The proposition ranges over such models. Its input format, accumulation format, and input rounding function determine all model-dependent quantities in the conclusion.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002
dependency_coverage.meaning: For v : Fin n → ℝ, this is the finite supremum of |v_i|, represented through nonnegative reals and converted back to ℝ. Thus it is the infinity norm max_i |v_i|; for n = 0 the fold returns 0.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies both positivity assumptions, the vector magnitudes in the scaling conditions, and the two infinity-norm factors on the right-hand side.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef003
dependency_coverage.meaning: The error E equals the scaled rounded quantity from D018 minus the exact real dot product Σ_i x_i y_i.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Its absolute value is the left-hand side of the asserted error bound.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef004
dependency_coverage.meaning: For u, g, θ, x, and y, it is (2u + u²)Σ_i |x_i||y_i| + 4nθ⁻¹g(1 + u + θ⁻¹g)‖x‖∞‖y‖∞.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: This is exactly the right-hand side of the conclusion, with u from D006, g from D005, and θ from D008.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef005
dependency_coverage.meaning: The input format's absolute-error allowance g at index t, defined by D014.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It appears in the second error term, both linearly and inside 1 + u + g/θ.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef006
dependency_coverage.meaning: The input format's relative-error allowance u at index t, equal to 2 raised to minus the input precision.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the coefficient 2u + u² and appears in the second error term.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef007
dependency_coverage.meaning: Admissible(θ,v,a) means that a = 2^k for some integer k, a > 0, and either v = 0 with a = 1, or v > 0 with θ/(2v) < a ≤ θ/v.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It restricts λ relative to ‖x‖∞ and μ relative to ‖y‖∞. Since both norms are assumed positive, only its second branch can hold.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef008
dependency_coverage.meaning: The scaling threshold θ is min(M_in, sqrt(M_acc/n)), where M_in and M_acc are the D013 maximum-magnitude quantities for the input and accumulation formats at t.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It controls the admissible intervals for λ and μ and occurs through θ⁻¹ in the bound.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef009
dependency_coverage.meaning: Projection of the model's second component, namely its accumulation format.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Its maximum-magnitude quantity contributes to θ.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef010
dependency_coverage.meaning: Projection of the model's first component, namely its input format.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It determines u, g, the input maximum magnitude, and the rounding function used in the computed quantity.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef011
dependency_coverage.meaning: Constructor for a model with input and accumulation formats satisfying p_in ≤ p_acc, e_min,acc ≤ e_min,in, and e_max,in ≤ e_max,acc. For each format, rounding has the form R(z) = z(1 + δ(z)) + η(z), with |δ(z)| ≤ u, |η(z)| ≤ g, and η(z)δ(z) = 0.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: These are intrinsic assumptions on every quantified model, including the input-rounding error law relevant to D018. The accumulation-rounding law is present in the model but not applied in D018.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef012
dependency_coverage.meaning: The absolute componentwise product sum Σ_i |x_i||y_i|.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It multiplies the coefficient 2u + u² in the first error term.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef013
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a format at t, the maximum-magnitude parameter M = 2^e_max(2 - 2u), where u = 2^(-p).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The input and accumulation instances determine the two arguments of the minimum defining θ.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef014
dependency_coverage.meaning: For precision p, minimum exponent e_min, and subnormal flag s, g equals 2^e_min/2 when s is false and 2^(-p)2^e_min when s is true.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: For the input format it defines the absolute-error allowance used in the rounding assumptions and final bound.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef015
dependency_coverage.meaning: For precision p, this is u = (1/2)^p = 2^(-p).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is the relative-error allowance for each format and, for the input format, the u used explicitly in the conclusion.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef016
dependency_coverage.meaning: The predicate that a real number is an integer power of two: there exists k ∈ ℤ such that a = 2^k. The integer exponent is fixed by the Real/Int power dependency D086.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It requires both scaling factors λ and μ to be powers of two.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef017
dependency_coverage.meaning: A proof object enabling the overloaded real numeral 2.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies numeral infrastructure for coefficients and denominators; it adds no mathematical hypothesis.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef018
dependency_coverage.meaning: A = λ⁻¹μ⁻¹ Σ_i R_in(t, λx_i)R_in(t, μy_i), where R_in is the model's input rounding function.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: This is the computed quantity compared with the exact dot product. Multiplication, summation, and inverse rescaling in this definition are exact real operations.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef019
dependency_coverage.meaning: For n and real bounds fmax and Fmax, it returns min(fmax, sqrt(Fmax/n)).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It combines the input and accumulation maximum-magnitude parameters into θ.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef020

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef021

dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Two such formats are stored in the model and determine u, g, maximum magnitudes, and θ.

binders: Universally quantified are a natural dimension n, an arbitrary index type ι, a mixed-precision rounding model indexed by ι, and an index t ∈ ι.
Universally quantified are two real vectors x,y : Fin n → ℝ.
Universally quantified are two real scaling factors λ and μ.
hypotheses: Each model format F has p_F(s) > 0 and e_min,F(s) ≤ e_max,F(s) for every s ∈ ι.
For every s ∈ ι, the model satisfies p_in(s) ≤ p_acc(s), e_min,acc(s) ≤ e_min,in(s), and e_max,in(s) ≤ e_max,acc(s).

For F equal to the input or accumulation format, the corresponding rounding data satisfy R_F(s,z) = z(1 + δ_F(s,z)) + η_F(s,z), |δ_F(s,z)| ≤ u_F(s), |η_F(s,z)| ≤ g_F(s), and η_F(s,z)δ_F(s,z) = 0 for every s ∈ ι and z ∈ ℝ.
Both vectors are nonzero in infinity norm: ‖x‖∞ > 0 and ‖y‖∞ > 0.
There exists k ∈ ℤ with λ = 2^k, λ > 0, and either ‖x‖∞ = 0 with λ = 1, or ‖x‖∞ > 0 with θ/(2‖x‖∞) < λ ≤ θ/‖x‖∞.
There exists l ∈ ℤ with μ = 2^l, μ > 0, and either ‖y‖∞ = 0 with μ = 1, or ‖y‖∞ > 0 with θ/(2‖y‖∞) < μ ≤ θ/‖y‖∞.
conclusions: |λ⁻¹μ⁻¹ Σ_i R_in(t,λx_i)R_in(t,μy_i) - Σ_i x_i y_i| ≤ (2u + u²)Σ_i |x_i||y_i| + 4nθ⁻¹g(1 + u + θ⁻¹g)‖x‖∞‖y‖∞.
mathematical_definitions: All sums and maxima range over i ∈ Fin n, equivalently i = 0,...,n-1.
For v : Fin n → ℝ, ‖v‖∞ = max_i |v_i|. The underlying finite-supremum definition returns 0 when n = 0.
For a format F at s, define u_F(s) = 2^(-p_F(s)) and M_F(s) = 2^e_max,F(s)(2 - 2u_F(s)).
For a format F at s, define g_F(s) = 2^e_min,F(s)/2 if its subnormal flag is false, and g_F(s) = u_F(s)2^e_min,F(s) if that flag is true.
In the conclusion, u = u_in(t), g = g_in(t), and θ = min(M_in(t), sqrt(M_acc(t)/n)).
The computed scaled quantity is A = λ⁻¹μ⁻¹ Σ_i R_in(t,λx_i)R_in(t,μy_i), and the exact comparison value is the real dot product x·y = Σ_i x_i y_i.
The error is E = A - x·y, and the componentwise absolute product sum is Σ_i |x_i||y_i|.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every positive dimension, every valid indexed mixed-precision rounding model, two nonzero real vectors, and positive integer-power-of-two scales that place each scaled vector's infinity norm between one half of θ and θ, the exact real sum of products of the individually input-rounded scaled coordinates, rescaled by λ⁻¹μ⁻¹, differs from the exact dot product by at most (2u + u²) times the absolute componentwise product sum plus 4n(g/θ)(1 + u + g/θ) times the product of the two infinity norms.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The proposition requires n > 0 and excludes both zero vectors. Consequently, the zero-norm, scale-equals-one branch in each admissibility hypothesis is unreachable here.
